transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I don’t feel any interest in the things I used to love—my art, my garden, even time with my family just feels flat. I just wake up feeling so weary, and nothing seems to matter to me anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been most days for at least two years, or is this a more recent change that started within the past few months?

It’s been building and sticking around for a little over two years now. It really started around the time my husband began traveling more for work and my kids became more independent, and it has just persisted since then.
Over the past two years, have you felt depressed or down most days, or is it mainly that you’ve lost interest and feel tired?

It’s actually a mix of both; I feel a complete loss of interest where I just stare at my painting canvas or seed packets and feel absolutely nothing, but I also have a heavy, sad feeling most days like a gray film is over everything. While my overall struggles have been going on for about two years, these specific heavy, empty phases have lasted for about seven months in total.
During the last seven months, has your low mood been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Yes, absolutely. During those low stretches over the last seven months, that heavy, sinking feeling has been there almost every single day from the moment I wake up. It easily lasts for weeks at a time where everything just feels completely gray and pointless.
Have you ever had a period of at least two full weeks during which you felt depressed or lost interest nearly every day, most of the day?

Yes, definitely. I've had stretches lasting much longer than two weeks where a heavy gray film covers everything and I completely lose interest in my painting, gardening, and family. In total over the last couple of years, those low periods have added up to about seven months.
Between those low periods, have you ever felt back to your usual self for at least a few months, or has the depressed/empty feeling been present most of the time for the past two years?

No, those empty feelings haven't been there the whole time, as they've only lasted about seven months in total over the last two years. I actually spend much more time in sped-up, high-energy phases that have been coming and going for about a year and eight months now. I even had a stretch last year where my mood felt relatively neutral, though I still heard the whispering and had those suspicious thoughts during that time.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did risky things like spending too much or acting impulsively?

Yes, for about a year and eight months now, I've had phases where I feel incredibly wired, giddy, and easily annoyed, getting by on just three or four hours of sleep. During these times, I talk really fast and rush around starting a dozen different projects all at once. These high-energy periods usually last for days or even weeks at a time before I eventually crash.

Have you ever heard voices or had suspicious beliefs like people were watching or talking about you when you were not in a depressed or high-energy episode, or do those symptoms only happen during mood episodes?

Yes, those things actually do happen even when my mood feels completely flat or neutral. Last year, there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't feeling particularly high or low, but I still heard the nighttime whispering and felt convinced my husband's trips were part of a test on me.
Have you ever had times when the hallucinations or suspicious beliefs lasted for at least 2 weeks even when your mood was not depressed, elevated, or irritable?

Yes, there was a stretch last year for about three weeks where my mood felt completely neutral, neither high nor low. Even during those weeks, I still heard the whispering at night and was convinced my husband's work trips were part of a test on me. It lasted that entire time despite my emotions being stable.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or suspicious beliefs even though you were not having any depression or manic symptoms at the same time?

Yes, absolutely. Last year I had a stretch of about three weeks where my mood felt completely neutral, with no highs or lows at all. Yet, during that entire time, I still heard the whispers in the hallway at night and remained convinced my husband's trips were some kind of test.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where your mood was abnormally high or irritable and you had much more energy than usual, with less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or very increased activity?

Yes, I've had those periods last for a week or more at a time over the past year and eight months. I get so wired and giddy, sleeping only three or four hours but waking up buzzing with my mind racing like a radio stuck between stations. I'll rush around starting a dozen different projects all at once, getting easily irritated, and then leave them all half-finished.

During your high-energy periods, have you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, or had psychosis like voices or strong paranoid beliefs that were clearly present while you were also manic?

I haven't ever been hospitalized, but my high-energy, wired phases definitely overlap with those strange experiences. When I'm racing around on almost no sleep, the whispering voices about my parenting are at their loudest, and my belief that my family is secretly testing me is at its strongest.
Have the hallucinations or suspicious beliefs ever lasted for at least 2 weeks when you were not having any depressed, manic, or irritable mood symptoms at all?

Yes, definitely. Last year I had a period of about three weeks where my mood felt completely normal and neutral, with no highs or lows. Even so, the whispering and the feeling that my family was testing me lasted through that entire time.
Have you ever had a manic episode that lasted at least 7 days and was severe enough to cause major problems, like needing hospitalization or being unable to function normally?

Yes, I've had those wired, high-energy phases last for a week or more at a time, coming and going for about a year and eight months now. While I have never been hospitalized, they cause major problems in my life because I let bills pile up, miss appointments, forget basic chores, and feel completely unable to hold a job or finish any projects.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever become so severely manic that you needed to be hospitalized, or had such extreme impairment that you could not care for yourself or function safely?

No, I've never been hospitalized or felt completely unable to survive or keep myself safe. However, I still struggle a lot to function, like letting bills pile up and forgetting basic chores around the house. I also end up leaving a massive mess of half-finished projects everywhere that I just can't seem to manage.
Have you ever had a manic episode so severe that you were hospitalized, or that your behavior became so extreme that you could not keep yourself safe or function at all?

No, I have never been hospitalized during those high-energy periods. While they definitely make my life messy and disorganized with all the half-finished projects, I don't think it has ever gotten quite that extreme or unsafe.
Have you ever had hallucinations or paranoid beliefs for at least 2 weeks when you were not having any depression or manic symptoms at all?

Yes, that actually did happen. Last year, there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood felt relatively neutral—neither high nor low—but I still heard the nighttime whispering and felt convinced my husband's work trips were part of a test on me.
Have you ever had a full manic episode that was severe enough to require hospitalization or cause you to be unable to function safely, or have your high-energy episodes never reached that level?

No, my high-energy phases have never reached the level of needing hospitalization or being completely unsafe. However, they still seriously disrupt my daily life because I let bills pile up, neglect chores, and leave a trail of half-finished projects everywhere. It makes me feel unable to hold down a job or function normally.
Have you ever had a full manic episode so severe that you needed hospitalization, or were your high-energy episodes severe but never that extreme?

While those high-energy episodes feel incredibly intense, disruptive, and leave me feeling exhausted and embarrassed, they have never been so extreme that I needed to be hospitalized. Seeing you today is actually my first real step in getting professional help for these struggles.
Have your high-energy periods ever become so severe that you were hospitalized or completely unable to keep yourself safe and function, or have they always been intense but not that extreme?

They are definitely very intense and disruptive, causing me to neglect bills, start dozens of unfinished projects, and strain my relationships with my family. However, I have never been hospitalized or felt completely unable to keep myself safe during those times.
Have you ever had a manic episode so severe that you needed to be hospitalized, or were your high-energy episodes intense but never that extreme?

No, I have never been hospitalized for those high-energy episodes. Even though they are intense—causing me to stay up all night feeling extremely wired and leaving projects half-finished—they have never reached the point of requiring hospital care, though they certainly cause a lot of strain at home.
Have your high-energy periods ever been so severe that you were hospitalized, or have they always been intense but not severe enough to require hospital care?
No, I've never been hospitalized for those high-energy periods. They do feel very intense and disruptive to my life at home, but it has never reached the point of needing hospital care.
Have your high-energy periods ever become so severe that you were hospitalized, or have they always been intense but not severe enough to require hospital care?

No, I have never been hospitalized during those high-energy times. They are definitely intense and cause a lot of disruption at home with all my unfinished projects, but it has never gotten to the point of needing hospital care.
Have your high-energy periods ever become so severe that you needed to be hospitalized, or have they always been intense but not severe enough to require hospital care?
No, I've never been hospitalized for those high-energy times. Even though they are extremely intense and disrupt my daily life, they've never gotten to the point of needing hospital care.
Have your high-energy periods ever been severe enough that you needed hospitalization or became completely unable to function safely, or have they always been intense but not that severe?

No, my high-energy periods have never been so severe that I needed hospitalization or couldn't keep myself safe. They are incredibly intense and cause a lot of chaos—like leaving a trail of half-finished projects and letting bills pile up—but they have never reached the level of needing hospital care.
Have your high-energy periods ever been severe enough to cause marked impairment in work or social functioning, even if you did not need hospitalization?

Yes, they have definitely caused major disruptions in my life. I've completely stopped going to my book club and art events, missed appointments, and let bills pile up. I also don't feel capable of holding down a job because I start so many projects that I can't finish and just end up completely exhausted.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever had symptoms severe enough to require hospitalization, or were they intense but never that severe?

No, those phases have never been severe enough to require hospitalization. Even though they are incredibly intense and overwhelming, causing me to neglect household chores and leave half-finished projects everywhere, I have never needed hospital care.
Have you ever had a manic episode so severe that you needed hospitalization, or have your high-energy periods always been intense but not severe enough to require hospital care?
I have never been hospitalized for my high-energy periods. While those times are definitely intense, I have always just stayed at home when they happen.
Have your high-energy periods ever caused you to become so severely impaired that you needed hospitalization, or have they always been intense but not severe enough to require hospital care?
No, I have never been hospitalized for those high-energy periods. They are still very intense and disruptive for me, but they have never reached the point of needing hospital care.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever become so severely impaired that you needed hospitalization or were unable to care for yourself safely, or have they been intense but not that severe?

No, those periods have never resulted in hospitalization, but they are still incredibly intense and overwhelming, leaving me buzzing on just a few hours of sleep while racing to start countless projects. They are highly disruptive rather than harmless, as I end up letting bills pile up, forgetting basic chores, and leaving a trail of half-finished projects that severely strain my relationships and daily life.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a clear schizoaffective disorder with both prominent mood episodes and psychotic symptoms. She reports recurrent manic episodes with decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, racing thoughts, increased goal-directed activity, and marked functional impairment, alongside depressive episodes with anhedonia, low mood, and fatigue. Psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions) persisted for at least 3 weeks during a period of neutral mood, establishing psychosis outside mood episodes. Because the manic syndrome is clearly present and there is no history of a full manic episode requiring hospitalization, the overall picture is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.2) rather than depressive type.
